A staccato of clicks can be heard in the canopy above, among the thick pine boughs of the colossal conifers that tower over the 
mountainous forests of Last Bloom and Amberdale. While they may look sinister in appearance, the ricatrillisk is nothing but benefi cial 
to the health of the Wealdwoods. Clinging to thick trunks it climbs upwards, sniffi ng out the rot and fungus that infects the oldest 
trees. Once it fi nds a sizable growth, it clings tightly to the wide trunk, munching through the tough exterior while its own chitinous 
hide protects it from aerial predators. Although a solitary fungivore, after mating season, its larvae will cling to the bodies of both male 
and female adults, as they clamber along the heights, depositing their young onto fungal growths to eat and grow as budding pupae. 
Class - Insecta • Genus Derived Evolution - Extatosoma • Niche - Specialist Arboreal Fungivore

Encountering Climbing to heights other creatures would have 
diffi culty reaching, the ricatrillisk is used to peaceful isolation. 
With little to lure the insect since its only interest is in the trees, 
this slow moving foliage-colored creature can be challenging to 
capture, but once found gripping tightly to the trunk, it's only a 
matter of fi nding a method to climb after it, or felling the tree.
